ai_show_review.summary: Ferocious Fillmore debut with epic Caution & St. Stephen
ai_show_review.blurb: The show opens and closes with a wild feedback sandwich framing a blistering 24‑minute “Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)”. Highlights include a searing Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence and the Alligator → Turn On Your Lovelight transition. While the audio is muddy, Garcia’s guitar cuts through and captures the band’s primal 1968 energy.
ai_show_review.review: On June 14, 1968 the Dead burst onto the Fillmore East stage with a set that still feels like a raw, unfiltered lightning strike. A feedback sandwich bookends the performance, leading straight into an incendiary The Eleven that rockets into Saint Stephen – a moment reviewers call “smoking” and “legendary”. The band then rolls through a ferocious 24‑minute Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks), punctuated by a wild Drums interlude before returning to the same theme and closing with feedback once more. Alligator segues seamlessly into Turn On Your Lovelight, showcasing the group’s willingness to swing from tight blues to free‑form psychedelia in one breath. Though the audience tape is muddy – drums are often lost and vocals buried – Garcia’s lead guitar remains crystal clear, soaring above the chaos and proving why this debut is still talked about by Deadheads today.

best_recording.reason: Captures the full set with the iconic feedback sandwich and relatively clearer guitar, making it the most complete listening experience despite lo‑fi tape limitations.

key_highlights: 24‑minute “Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)” that dominates the second half of the set
Feedback sandwich framing the entire performance adds a wild, experimental edge
Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence is described as smoking and legendary
Alligator seamlessly transitions into Turn On Your Lovelight, showing the band’s genre‑bending flow

band_performance.Jerry: Dominant throughout; his guitar is loud, often the only clearly audible instrument and described as ‘on another plane’ or blazing.
band_performance.Phil: Bass is largely lost in the mix; occasional fills are noted but overall barely audible.
band_performance.Bob: Vocals and harp are buried under the tape noise, with only faint presence during Caution.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are muffled or inaudible for much of the show, making rhythm hard to discern.
band_performance.Billy: Same as Mickey – drum parts are muddy and often lost in the recording.
